projects.title: Ver Análisis
projects.summary: A Spanish-only proof of concept that gives clinics a straightforward way to publish diagnostic reports and lets patients securely open, share, and print them from a unique link.
projects.whyBuilt: Diagnostic reports are often delivered through disconnected channels that make it harder for clinics to keep a consistent identity and for patients to access their results. I built Ver Análisis to explore a small, direct reporting flow: clinicians create a branded clinic, publish a report with its scans, and immediately receive a patient-ready URL and QR code.

capabilities: Lets doctors create clinics with their own logo and brand colour before preparing reports.
Captures the patient details, report content, date, clinician, and scan images in one reporting workflow.
Publishes each completed report with a unique patient URL and a QR code that can be shared through WhatsApp.
Gives patients a Spanish-only report page where they can review scan thumbnails, inspect individual images, share the link, and print a two-page report.
technicalHighlights: Built the proof of concept with React and Tailwind CSS, keeping the doctor workflow and patient-facing report experience in the same web application.
Uses Firebase Firestore for clinic and report data, with Firebase Storage for uploaded diagnostic scan images.
Uses Jest to cover the application behaviour as the reporting workflow evolves.
keyDecisions: Used a unique report code and direct URL so a patient can open a result without navigating a clinic portal.
Made clinic branding configurable at the clinic level, allowing one product to support distinct practices without duplicating the reporting flow.
Kept the patient experience focused on reviewing, sharing, and printing the completed report rather than exposing administrative controls.
projects.status: Proof of concept. The clinician reporting, branded clinic, patient report, image viewing, QR sharing, and print flows are implemented.

projects.title: Luno Buy & Sell Flow Renovation
projects.summary: A frontend-driven renovation of the buy and sell journeys for Luno, a crypto fintech product, making high-stakes transactions clearer and more focused.
projects.whyBuilt: The existing purchase journey had accumulated screens and separated card payment into another browser tab. As the sole web engineer, I rebuilt the experience around a clearer flow that kept customers in context from entering an amount through to confirmation.
capabilities: Guides customers through clearer crypto purchase and sale journeys built from a shared component library.
Reduces the buy journey by two screens by condensing information without removing the context customers need to complete a purchase.
Replaces a four-screen, separate-tab card-payment journey with an in-context modal that closes after confirmed payment and returns the customer to the end-of-flow screen.
Applies the established buy-flow pattern to a sell-flow MVP delivered in about three weeks.
technicalHighlights: Built frontend-driven Angular flows with TypeScript and RxJS, after contributing the required shared components to the company library.
Used an AI-first delivery approach: the buy flow established a reusable example, while the sell MVP was accelerated with Claude Code.
Added analytics, feature flags, and automated coverage with Playwright, Karma, and Jasmine.
keyDecisions: Ran the buy-flow release as an A/B test to validate whether a shorter journey improved the purchase experience; the sell flow reused the proven pattern without a separate experiment.
Kept card payment inside the flow so confirmation returns customers to the right screen instead of losing their context in a separate tab.
Invested in shared components first so the two flows could be assembled consistently and delivered faster.
projects.status: Shipped at Luno. The buy-flow A/B test validated the shorter purchase journey.

projects.title: Luno Dynamic Send & Receive Flows
projects.summary: Backend-driven, country-specific regulatory journeys for sending and receiving crypto, designed to keep Luno compliant with local requirements.
projects.whyBuilt: Send and receive journeys needed to adapt to different local regulations without creating a separate frontend flow for every country. As the sole web engineer, I built a flexible presentation layer that could safely assemble the appropriate journey from backend-provided definitions.
capabilities: Presents compliant send and receive journeys that adapt to country-specific rules.
Builds a Dynamic Flow from backend-provided JSON that identifies the screen type and supplies its content.
Renders either a predefined screen or a generic composition of shared components, depending on the backend definition.
technicalHighlights: Implemented an Angular and TypeScript presentation layer for backend-driven screen definitions, using RxJS to coordinate dynamic state.
Used the company component library to keep dynamically assembled flows consistent with the wider product.
Added analytics, feature flags, and automated coverage with Playwright, Karma, and Jasmine.
keyDecisions: Kept regulatory decision-making in backend definitions so country rules could vary without duplicating frontend journeys.
Used a small set of predefined and generic screen patterns to handle variation while keeping the customer experience consistent.
Made experimentation and observability part of the flow architecture through feature flags and analytics.

projects.title: TechSoup AngularJS to React Modernisation
projects.summary: A staged modernisation of internal applications at TechSoup, a nonprofit technology provider serving organisations worldwide, moving legacy AngularJS experiences to React.
projects.whyBuilt: Internal applications needed a more maintainable frontend foundation and a practical migration path away from AngularJS. As JavaScript lead engineer, I established that foundation before migrating applications one by one, so teams could modernise without a disruptive rewrite programme.
capabilities: Provides a repeatable path for moving internal applications from AngularJS to React.
Modernises styling from plain CSS to Bootstrap and SCSS, making implementation easier to extend and maintain.
Improves and simplifies legacy AngularJS code while applications wait to be migrated.
Supports a gradual, application-by-application migration instead of a high-risk platform rewrite.
technicalHighlights: Led the JavaScript foundation work across React and AngularJS applications.
Introduced Bootstrap, SCSS, and Tailwind CSS tooling to make styling more consistent and practical to develop.
Used Jest to support a safer migration path as individual applications moved to React.
keyDecisions: Established shared styling and code-quality foundations before migrating applications, so each migration built on a more maintainable base.
Improved legacy AngularJS code rather than treating it as untouchable, reducing friction during the transition.
Migrated incrementally to limit delivery risk for internal teams.

projects.title: TechSoup TypeScript Endpoint Library
projects.summary: An internal TypeScript library that gives applications only the endpoint data they need, reducing repeated data trimming and making API consumption easier for development teams.
projects.whyBuilt: Endpoints often returned more data than individual applications needed, leaving teams to repeatedly trim responses and making correct usage harder for junior developers. As JavaScript lead engineer, I created a shared library that made the intended data shape the default.
capabilities: Reduces endpoint responses to the fields requested through the endpoint parameters.
Removes repeated response-trimming work from consuming applications.
Gives developers a simpler, safer way to consume shared endpoint data.
technicalHighlights: Built the internal library in TypeScript with Jest coverage.
Used Rollup to publish CommonJS output for AngularJS applications and ESM output for React applications.
Created one shared endpoint-consumption layer for applications at different stages of the frontend modernisation.
keyDecisions: Applied response selection inside the shared library so consumers received only the data their endpoint parameters requested.
Published both CommonJS and ESM builds to support the existing AngularJS estate alongside newer React applications.
Optimised the library for clear defaults so less-experienced developers could use endpoints without manual response shaping.
